questions.question: Define mechanical advantage, state the trade it involves, give how it is found for each mechanism studied, and calculate it for the model crane from crank to magnet.
questions.expected_answer: Mechanical advantage is load divided by effort, with no unit, and because no mechanism gives out more work than it receives, multiplying force by a factor makes the effort move that many times further. It is found for a lever by effort distance over load distance from the pivot, for a crank by handle radius over drum radius, for a wheel and axle by wheel radius over axle radius, for a pulley system by the number of rope sections supporting the load, for gears by driven teeth over driver teeth, and for hydraulics by large piston area over small piston area. In the crane a 75 millimetre handle on a 12 millimetre drum gives about six, the fixed tip pulley gives one, and there is no further mechanism, so the total is six; a 60 gram load needs about 10 grams at the handle, and a movable pulley at the magnet would double this to twelve at the cost of twice the turns.

questions.question: Describe the three ways a frame structure fails and the ways each is prevented, with reference to the crane's members, joints and base.
questions.expected_answer: Members bend or buckle, joints rotate so the frame folds into a parallelogram, and the whole structure tips. Bending is resisted by shaping members into tubes, L, U or box sections so material lies away from the centre of the section, and buckling by keeping compression members short and braced; the mast should be a tube or box, the arm a tube or triangular section. Folding is prevented by triangulation, adding a diagonal or a card gusset to every rectangular panel so it becomes two triangles that cannot change shape. Tipping is prevented by a wide base, the mast near the centre, a counterweight such as the cells at the back of the base, and a low centre of gravity. Joints are made by overlapping, tabs or gussets so glue works over an area, skewers pass through two card layers, and the arm-to-mast joint is sleeved or gusseted and tied back to the mast top.

questions.question: Explain how to apply both revision sheets to a chosen crane sketch by walking the load path and the effort path, and what should be marked on the sketch.
questions.expected_answer: Walk the load path backwards from the magnet: the string pulls on the arm tip, the arm presses and tries to rotate at the mast joint, the mast presses on the base, and the base tries to lift at the back; at each step check that the mechanism keeps its advantage and the structure resists its failure, giving a light grooved pulley, a tube arm braced to the mast top, a gusseted joint, a tube or lattice mast and a double base with the cells behind. Walk the effort path forward from the hand: firm right-angle handle, small drum with one layer of string, string straight up the mast and over the pulley; total advantage six and effort equal to load over six. The sketch is marked with the chain of numbers and total on one side and the stiffening labels, tube, gusset, diagonal, counterweight, in a second colour on the other, and kept in the design folder, since the rubric rewards understanding of both.
